## Decision record: what the engine face promises, and what its receipts look like

::: {.callout .callout-note}
**Decision.** CS-16 is a witness, not a specification: it freezes what the
exported `ms_ard()` factory and the `MsArd` constructor actually
adjudicate over planted calls, so future drift speaks immediately. It
commits only machine-stable facts: the error CLASS always, and the message
CLAUSES verbatim -- every one of them. The face is pure R with no path,
clock, RNG or locale in its output, so the ledger was DET-proved
byte-stable across probe reruns and no arm needed the `stable3`
bullet-subset posture that CS-13/CS-14 required for their file paths.
:::

### The face

`ms_ard(a0, b0, tol, max_iter, seed)` is the exported constructor of the
ARD-NMF engine descriptor: an S7 class (eleven ALL-defaulted properties,
`label` speaking "ARD-NMF (SignatureAnalyzer semantics)") behind TWO
admission gates -- the S7 property gates and the validators (the shared
engine validator, then `msuiter_validate_ard`). CS-16 fires 57 observation
arms at it plus seven boundary pairs: 40 law arms, 9 acceptance specs,
8 precedence discriminators, 7 degenerate pairs (14 rows), 9 scalars. The
committed lane replays every arm live: the law file adjudicates 246
expectations across 10 units (0 failed, 0 errors, 0 warnings) and the
runner rails every row against the frozen block before any witness byte
is written.

### The double gate -- measured, and its surprise third voice

The property gates and the validator split is committed as measured: of
the 40 law arms, 12 die as `simpleError` at the property gates ("<char>
is not <integer> or <double>" for the five numeric hyper-properties,
"@params must be <list>", "@deterministic must be <logical>"), 26 speak
the validator's own `msuiter_error_engine`, and TWO arms uncovered a
third voice: a length-2 vector for `a0` or `seed` passes the property
gate (numeric vector), reaches the validator's whole-number clause -- and
dies inside the abort machinery itself as `msuiter_error_internal`:
"msuiter_abort: bullet 'i' must be a non-empty string", because the
got:/format(v) bullet vectorises with the two-element value. The face
still refuses the input; it refuses it from the plumbing, and the witness
records that too rather than laundering it.

### The laws the face demonstrates

- **Shared engine laws.** The name must be a single lower-case snake_case
  string; the mode is one of {extract, fit}; `params` must be a list --
  and MEASURED, the "(named)" in the clause is permissive: a fully
  unnamed list passes (the `names()` short-circuit), a PARTIALLY named
  one is refused. `deterministic` is a bare TRUE/FALSE; `packages` a
  character vector without NA and no empty names; `label` a single
  string, empty allowed.
- **The ARD priors.** `a0`/`b0` must be single finite numbers > 0 (zero,
  negative, Inf, NaN, NA each refused with the got:/value bullet); `tol`
  the same positive-finite law -- closing at exactly the kernel's domain,
  so an R-side pass can never hand the Rust kernel an illegal tolerance;
  `max_iter` a single positive WHOLE number; `seed` a whole number in
  [0, 2^31 - 1], the boundary pair committing both ends (0 and
  2147483647 accepted, -1 and 2147483648 refused).
- **Precedence.** Eight discriminators with fires AND anti anchors:
  name before mode, mode before params, deterministic before packages,
  packages before label (the shared roster, and a defective object whose
  SHARED fields are wrong proves the shared validator runs over the ARD
  fields), then a0 before b0, tol before max_iter, max_iter before seed.
- **The format contract.** The accepted rendering is the format method's
  own line, `<MsEngine> ARD-NMF (SignatureAnalyzer semantics) (ard) |
  mode: extract | deterministic ...`, carried verbatim in the specs
  witness; the replay-identity spec welds two renders of one object with
  `==`.

### The receipts

| receipt | committed bytes |
|---|---|
| `cs16_specs.tsv` | 9 accepted arms: class token `s7:msuiter::MsArd` plus the shape rendering (roster, hyper values, format line), and the `s7:character` replay identity |
| `cs16_laws.tsv` | 40 arms: class census MEASURED 26 validator + 12 property-gate + 2 internal-plumbing, every clause verbatim, every mode `reject` |
| `cs16_precedence.tsv` | 8 discriminators, each with its fires anchor PRESENT and its anti anchor ABSENT in the live message |
| `cs16_degenerates.tsv` | 7 boundary pairs (14 rows): max_iter floor, seed floor and ceiling, tol floor, empty label, mode domain, finite a0 ceiling -- hi accepts, lo rejects, by the committed law |
| `cs16_scalars.tsv` | 9 keys: the validator's own class token, five clause re-fires, the canonical shape, and both RNG-purity rails (the adjudication core never seeds) |

The 71-row class census (41 engine, 12 simpleError, 2 internal, 15
MsArd, 1 character) is recomputed from the frozen vectors inside the law
file -- a silent class shift reddens the lane, not the reader. All five
witnesses byte-reproduce on consecutive runner invocations, the plant and
spec corpora hash identically under BOTH governed SHA-256 kernels
(`.ms_fit_sha256` and digest), and the lane never touches the RNG, the
network, the benchmark driver, the declined calibration family, the
registry face, or any unexported internal (banned-word rails over the
hand-written region, marker-scoped and grepped).

### What the lane-building itself caught (the honest section)

The live replay is not decoration -- it killed an entire defect family
before one witness byte was trusted. (1) The minter's thunk-body
extractor took the LAST slot of a parsed function literal; on this base
that slot is an extra NULL, so all 57 arm texts minted as the string
"NULL" -- and both existing self-checks passed VACUOUSLY (parse("NULL")
is one expression; the double-mint determinism only proved the garbage
was stable). The live-replay mirror caught it as an arm rejecting with
`@params` on NULL. The extractor now pins slot [[3]] by measurement and
every arm text must speak a face token to mint. (2) The fire wrapper
projected `$v` off a tryCatch result that had taken the ERROR branch --
a condition object has no `$v`, so rejects were silently demoted to
accepts-of-NULL; fixed by branching on `inherits(., "error")` first.
(3) The fires-anchor derivation ran `regexpr` over a VECTOR and pulled
`attr(., "match.start")`, which is NULL there, feeding
`ifelse(logical(0), .)` -- the whole 8-entry anchor vector evaporated to
`character(0)` and emit minted an empty roster silently; the runner's own
fire-check died on the invalid pattern, and the minter now asserts each
fires anchor is a substring of its own message. (4) Three fork-semantics
rails fell over loudly instead of quietly: `vapply` refuses
logical-to-character coercion (the fires/anti columns are minted as
"TRUE"/"FALSE" strings at source), `vapply`'s names attribute made
`identical()` reddle against the nameless witness columns (row builders
now strip), and `grepl` takes only pattern element one of a vector
pattern (face-token guards speak three explicit tests). (5) The
banned-word rails initially hit the face's OWN quoted bytes inside the
frozen block (the internal clause names msuiter_abort; the packages
clause cites required_pkgs()) -- rails govern the hand-written region;
the minted regions are observed data, sliced out before the absence
scan, with marker integrity itself rail-checked. (6) The governance-file
surgery caught its own tooling twice: a sub() backreference landed a raw
0x01 control byte into the sealed row, and the line-multiset guard
refused two successive editor bugs of mine before letting the file
settle. The T0 seal moved 624 -> 625 with the generator's refusal
witnessed verbatim (the DEFECT line naming 625 against the sealed 624)
before the deliberate re-seal, per the budget law; the reified manifest
carries 109 files, the new law file on shard 5, byte-deterministic on
re-mint.

### Provenance

The frozen block and the shared code block in both hosts are minted
mechanically from the audited probe ledger (audit green: 57 arms, 14
degen rows, 9 scalars, 8/8 anti anchors); neither is ever hand-edited in
place. The plants' canonical texts hash to the committed dual-kernel
checksum; reifying the lane reproduces every witness byte for byte.
Differentiation from CS-12 (the engine-spec factory): CS-12 adjudicated
the SPEC-CONSTRUCTION factory surface; CS-16 adjudicates the descriptor
CLASS itself -- its property gates, its validator chain and the
abort-plumbing class beneath both.

### Gate forensics -- one self-caught leg defect and one exempted NOTE

The first full local burn reddened inside the vignette build: the new
scenarios leg reached for two precedence-witness columns that the committed
TSV never carried (`fires_anchor`/`anti_anchor` live only in the frozen
roster, and the vignette cannot source it -- self-containedness law). On this
base a missing data.frame column reads NULL and surfaced at the call site as
an invalid `pattern` argument. The fix re-expresses the precedence
adjudication over committed bytes only -- witness-row equality
(`identical(pr$msg, sh)`) plus literals read off the table dump -- and both
the standalone render and a direct chunk evaluation print all seven
adjudications TRUE before the gate was re-ignited. The parse-only pre-check
passed while render caught it: the pre-ignition render gate is mandatory
procedure, not the full burn's job.

The second burn completed clean (exit 0) but its Status carried a second
NOTE: `checking for future file timestamps ... unable to verify current
time`. Forensics located the carrier (`tools:::.check_packages`): the probe
verifies mtimes against an EXTERNAL clock fetched over HTTP from
worldclockapi.com, which currently answers empty on both endpoints, so the
probe self-declares inability. It reproduced identically across two full
burns while the same posture said OK earlier the same day -- the external
service changed state, not the tree -- and every CS-16 mtime is proven
strictly past. The sealed baseline stays the frozen 2W/1N; the NOTE receives
a documented environmental exemption, evidence-anchored, reported not
suppressed: a probe that admits it could not verify never becomes a green.
